title: Sunny and the Sleepy Wombat | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the little quokka meets old Basil the wombat, who is getting ready for his daytime sleep just as the stars come out — and his gentle explanation of wombat ways makes Sunny feel perfectly happy about her own bedtime. A warm story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The first stars were just appearing in the evening sky, soft and far away, like sleepy eyes blinking open one by one. The bush had grown warm and golden, and Sunny the little quokka was following a familiar track through the trees when she nearly tripped over a very large, very round, very grey bottom sticking out of the ground.

"Oh!" said Sunny.

"Hmph," said the bottom. And then, slowly, the rest of old Basil the wombat appeared — shuffling backward out of his burrow, his small ears flat, his wide nose twitching.

"Good evening, Basil," said Sunny politely.

Basil blinked his small dark eyes. "Good evening, little one. Or good morning, depending on how you look at it." He yawned — a wide, slow, ancient sort of yawn — and began to pat the earth around his burrow door, getting everything just right.

"Are you going to sleep?" Sunny asked, surprised. "But the stars are just coming out!"

"Ah," said Basil, in a low rumbling voice, "that is exactly right. The stars come out, and I go in. That is the wombat way. We sleep when the sun is up, and we explore when the moon is out."

Sunny thought about this for a moment. "So we are the opposite," she said.

"Exactly opposite," said Basil warmly. "You sleep at night. I sleep in the day. And the bush is never lonely, because someone is always awake."

Sunny liked that very much. She felt something settle quietly inside her — a warm, satisfied feeling, like a question answered.

"Goodnight, Basil," she said softly.

"Sleep well, little one," he said.

And Sunny went home to her nest, tucked herself in, and was asleep before the moon had even climbed above the trees.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, Basil. Goodnight, little one.
